function.name: read
function.description: Read a text file. The result shows each line as the line number, a tab, and the text. The line number and the tab are not part of the file. For a large file, use offset and limit to read one part. Use it in place of cat, head, tail, or Get-Content in bash. When you need several files, read them all in one reply with several read calls. It also reads PDF, Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), and Excel (.xlsx) files as text with numbered parts: paragraphs [P1], table cells, slides and shapes [2.1], and cells such as B4. Use office_edit to change a Word, PowerPoint, or Excel file. It shows a PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP image to a model that accepts images.

path.description: File path, relative to the project folder.

offset.description: The first line to read. Line 1 is the first line.

limit.description: The maximum number of lines to read. Default 2000.

pages.description: For a PDF: the pages to read, for example 1-5 or 2,7. Default: all.

function.name: glob
function.description:
Find files by a name pattern, for example **/*.py or src/**/*.ts. A pattern with no / matches the file name in each folder. The newest files come first.

Usage notes:
- It shows at most 200 files. If there are more, use a narrower pattern.
- To find text in files, use grep.
- Use it in place of find, ls, or dir in bash.
- When you need several patterns, make several glob calls in one reply.

path.description: The folder to search. Default: the project folder.

function.name: grep
function.description:
Search the content of files with a regular expression.

Output modes:
- output=files (default) lists the files that match.
- output=content shows the matching lines as path:line:text. Add context to see lines around each match.
- output=count shows the number of matching lines in each file.

Usage notes:
- Use it in place of grep, rg, findstr, or Select-String in bash.
- The pattern is a regular expression. Escape special characters, for example interface\{\} or foo\(.
- Use glob to limit the search, for example *.py. To find files by name, use the glob tool.
- It shows at most 200 files or 300 lines. If there are more, use a narrower pattern, path, or glob.
- After you find a match, use read to see the code around it.

path.description: A file or folder to search. Default: the project folder.

glob.description: Search only files that match this glob, for example *.py.

ignore_case.description: Ignore upper and lower case. Default false.

context.description: Lines to show before and after each match (content only).

function.name: edit
function.description:
Replace an exact string in an existing file.

Use it to change part of a file. To create a file or to replace all its content, use write. For Word, PowerPoint, or Excel files, use office_edit.

Usage notes:
- Read the file with the read tool before you edit it. The tool rejects an edit of a file that you did not read in this session, or that changed after the read.
- old_string must match the file exactly, with the same spaces and indentation. Do not copy the line numbers and the tab that the read tool puts before each line.
- old_string must occur one time in the file. If it occurs more times, add lines around it, or set replace_all to true to change each occurrence.
- If the edit fails with "old_string was not found", read the file again and copy the exact text.
- Make small, targeted edits. Do not replace a full file with edit.
- To make several changes to one file, make several edit calls.

path.description: File path, relative to the project folder.

function.name: write
function.description:
Create a file, or replace all the content of a file. The folders are created if necessary.

Usage notes:
- To change part of an existing file, use edit. Edit is safer, and the diff is smaller.
- Before you replace an existing file, read it. The tool rejects a replace of a file that you did not read in this session.
- Do not create documentation or README files unless the user asks for them.
- Do not use bash with echo or a redirect (>) to create a file. Use this tool.

path.description: File path, relative to the project folder.

content.description: The full content of the file.

function.name: bash
function.description:
Run a command with bash in the project folder. Each call starts a new shell in the project folder, so a cd does not stay for the next call.

Use it for commands that have no tool: git, package managers, tests, builds, and scripts.

Do not use it for these jobs. Use the tool instead:
- Read a file: use read, not cat, head, tail, or Get-Content.
- Find files by name: use glob, not find, ls, or dir.
- Find text in files: use grep, not grep, rg, findstr, or Select-String.
- Change a file: use edit or write, not sed, awk, echo, or a redirect (>).
- Talk to the user: write text in your reply, not echo.

Usage notes:
- The default timeout is 120 seconds, and the maximum is 600 seconds. For a long build, test run, or watcher, set run_in_background and read the output later with task_output.
- Do not run commands that wait for input. Use flags such as --yes or -y.
- Do not start servers that do not stop, unless you use run_in_background.
- Long output is cut, and the end is kept. Errors are usually at the end.
- When commands do not depend on each other, make several bash calls in one reply.
- Put quotes around paths that have spaces.
- Before you delete or move files, check the paths.
- Read the exit code and the output before you say that a command worked.

run_in_background.description: Run the command as a background task and return at once, for a long build, test run, or watcher. Read its output later with task_output. Optional.

description.description: What the command does, in 3 to 8 words, in the past tense, for the user. For example: Listed the skill files. Optional.

function.name: office_edit
function.description:
Change a Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), or Excel (.xlsx) file, or make a new one with create: true. Read the file first: the read tool numbers its parts. Give a list of edits; they apply in order, then the file is saved once. Each edit has an 'op':
Word: replace {find, replace}; insert_paragraph {after (paragraph number, 0 for the start), text, style?}; set_paragraph {index, text, style?}; delete_paragraph {index}; set_cell {table, row, col, text}; add_table {rows: [[text, ...], ...]}.
PowerPoint: replace {find, replace, slide?}; add_slide {title?, body? (lines), layout? (name or number), position?}; delete_slide {slide}; set_text {slide, shape, text}; set_notes {slide, text}.
Excel: set {cell, value, sheet?} (a value that starts with = is a formula); set_rows {start, rows: [[value, ...], ...], sheet?}; add_sheet {name}; rename_sheet {sheet, name}; delete_sheet {sheet}.
Numbers start at 1. A replace keeps the formatting when the text is in one run.
This tool is for small changes. To make a formatted document, a deck, or a workbook with formulas, or for tracked changes, comments, charts, or a template, load the docx, pptx, or xlsx skill first.

path.description: The .docx, .pptx, or .xlsx file, relative to the project folder.

create.description: True to make a new, empty document first.

edits.description: The edits, in order. Each is an object with 'op' and its fields.

function.name: show_document
function.description: Open a PDF (.pdf) or Word (.docx) file of the project in the Preview pane of the app, so that the user can look at it. Use it when the user asks to see a document, or after you make or change a document that the user must check. This tool does not give you the text: use read for that.

path.description: The path of the .pdf or .docx file, relative to the project.

function.name: show_visual
function.description:
Show an interactive visual in the chat: an HTML fragment, or one raw <svg> element. Use it for a diagram, a chart, a small demo, or a set of choices with buttons. The user sees it below your message. Follow these rules:
- Give a fragment only. Do not write <!DOCTYPE>, <html>, <head>, or <body>.
- Use these CSS variables for all colors and fonts. They change with the light and the dark theme: --color-text, --color-text-muted, --color-surface, --color-surface-2, --color-border, --color-accent, --color-accent-text, --color-success, --color-danger, --color-warning, --font-sans, --font-mono, --radius. Example: color: var(--color-text). Do not use fixed colors for text, lines, or backgrounds.
- Use a flat style: no gradients, no large shadows. The page background is transparent.
- Do not use vh units. The frame gets the height of its content.
- Scripts and styles can load only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, and unpkg.com. fetch and other network calls do not work.
- Call sendPrompt(text) in a button click to send text as the next prompt of the user.
- Keep the code short. Do not repeat the visual in your text reply.
- Optional: 'loading_messages', 1 to 4 short lines (about 5 words) that show while the visual loads. For a serious topic, keep them plain. The title is also the file name when the user downloads the visual.

title.description: A short snake_case name for the visual, for example loader_options.

code.description: The HTML fragment or the <svg> element.

loading_messages.description: Optional. 1 to 4 short lines that show while the visual loads.

function.name: send_file
function.description: Send files to the user: each file shows as a card in the chat. Use it for a deliverable that the user must see, for example a report, a chart image, an HTML page, or a built file. Do not send scratch files or each small change of a file. The files must exist in the project. 'display': "render" opens the first file in a pane of the app now (a PDF, a Word file, an image, an HTML page, or a text file); "attach" shows a card that the user opens in another app (for example a spreadsheet). Leave it out to let the app decide by the file type. 'status': "proactive" when you send the file on your own initiative and the user must see it now (the app shows a notification); else "normal". Add a 'caption' of one line when it helps.

files.description: The paths of the files, relative to the project or absolute.

caption.description: Optional. One short line about the files.

function.name: artifact
function.description: Publish an HTML page as an artifact: a page that the user opens from a card in the chat, in the Browser pane of the app. Use it for a report, a dashboard, an explainer, or a small app that the user keeps or shares, not for a quick look (use show_visual for that). Write the page to a .html file first, then publish it. The page must be complete: inline CSS and scripts, or scripts from cdnjs.cloudflare.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, or unpkg.com with an exact version. It must work at phone width and in light and dark mode. To update an artifact, publish the same file again, or give its 'id'. Actions: publish (default), list, read, delete.

file_path.description: publish: the .html file of the page.

title.description: publish: a name of 2 to 4 words. Default: the <title> of the page.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the card.

id.description: publish: the artifact to update. read, delete: the artifact.

function.name: update_plan
function.description: Show the user your plan for a task of more than one step, as a list under your message. Send the whole list each time: short steps (at most 7 words) in order, each with a status: pending, in_progress, or completed. Keep exactly one step in_progress while you work. Call it at the start of the task, again as soon as each step finishes (before you start the next step), and when the plan changes. Do not mark many steps completed at the end. After the user interrupts you or gives a new instruction, send the new whole list. Do not use it for a one-step answer.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1 to 12 steps).

content.description: The step, in a few words.

function.name: wrap_up
function.description: At the end of a turn in which you changed files, ran commands, or did work of more than one step, show the user a short recap in a box: what is now true and what is not done or not checked. 2 or 3 short sentences, about 40 words, 300 characters or less. Do not list each check or step that you did: the details go in your final answer. When the next move is the user's decision, add one short question in 'ask' (100 characters or less), and one or two answer buttons in 'actions': the first is your recommendation. A button has a label of 1 to 3 words, and a message that it sends as the user's next prompt. Call it once, as the last tool call of the turn, then write your final answer. Before wrap_up, call update_plan with each finished step completed. Do not use it for a short answer to a question.

recap.description: 2 or 3 short sentences, 300 characters or less: what changed, and what is not done.

ask.description: Optional: one short question for a decision of the user, 100 characters or less.

actions.description: Optional: 1 or 2 answer buttons. The first is your recommendation.

message.description: The prompt that the click sends. Default: the label.

function.name: web_fetch
function.description: Fetch a web page and read it as text. HTML becomes text in the Markdown form, with the links. It also reads JSON, plain text, and PDF files, and shows an image to a model that accepts images. A long page comes in parts: use offset to read the next part. A page that you fetched in the last 15 minutes comes from a cache. A redirect to another host does not continue: call web_fetch again with the new URL. Do not use it for pages of the dev servers: use the preview tools.

url.description: A full http or https URL.

offset.description: The first character to read. Default 0.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web. The result lists the title, the URL, and a short text of each page. Use web_fetch to read a page. Use it for information after your training data, for example new versions and docs. In your answer, give the URLs of the pages that you used, in a list with the title "Sources:".

allowed_domains.description: Show only results from these domains. Optional.

blocked_domains.description: Do not show results from these domains. Optional.

count.description: The number of results, 1 to 20. Default 8.

function.name: ask_user_question
function.description: Ask the user 1 to 4 questions while you work, each with 2 to 4 options. Use it when you must know a choice of the user to continue, for example between two designs, or to make a vague request clear. Do not use it for a question that the code or the docs can answer. The user can also type another answer. Put your recommended option first, and add " (Recommended)" to its label. To compare concrete things (a layout mockup, a code snippet, a diagram), give an option a 'preview': the card shows it next to the options in a monospace box. The user can add notes to the answer. The result gives the answers and the notes.

question.description: The full question. End it with a question mark.

header.description: A short label, 12 characters or less.

preview.description: Optional. Text that the card shows when the user looks at this option: an ASCII mockup, a code snippet, or a short comparison. Monospace, Markdown code fences allowed.

multiSelect.description: True: the user can pick more than one option.

function.name: exit_plan_mode
function.description: In plan mode, give the user your plan for approval when it is complete. The plan is Markdown: the steps, and the files that each step changes. The user accepts it (the mode changes and you start the work), asks for changes (you get the feedback and stay in plan mode), or rejects it. Use it only to plan a task that changes files, not after research only. When plan mode is off, do not call it.

function.name: memory
function.description: Save, read, or delete a memory that stays between sessions. action 'save' writes one fact (name, description, type, content) and updates the index MEMORY.md. A save with an existing name replaces that memory. action 'read' gives a memory, 'delete' removes it, and 'list' gives the index. For a feedback or project memory, end the content with a 'Why:' line and a 'How to apply:' line.

name.description: A short kebab-case slug, for example user-role.

description.description: For save: one line that tells when the memory is useful.

function.name: conversation_search
function.description: Search the past sessions of this project for relevant details: earlier decisions, requests, and answers. Use it when the user refers to an earlier conversation, or when context from an earlier session will help. The query is a few keywords. The result gives the title and the date of each session, with the parts that match.

function.name: start_session
function.description: Start a new session that does a separate task in the background. The sidebar shows the new session nested under this session. The user can open it, give it instructions, or stop it. Use this tool only for a task of its own that ends in its own result, for example a separate change, a branch, or a pull request, and only when the user asks for it or agrees to it. Do not use it for a small task or for a part of the current task: do that work here, or use the agent tool. The new session works in the project folder of this session, with the model and the permission mode of this session. This session does not get the result of the new session. After the start, tell the user the title of the new session.

title.description: A short title for the sidebar, for example 'Add nested sessions to the sidebar'.

prompt.description: The full task. The new session has no memory of this conversation: give the goal, the files, the constraints, and what done looks like.

worktree.description: True: the new session works in a new git worktree of the project, on its own branch. Use it when the work can touch the same files as this session. Default: false.

function.name: session_read
function.description: Read another session of this project: its title, its first prompt, and its last messages. Use an id of the session list note. Use it when the user refers to the work of another session, and before offer_session when you must know which session fits the task.

session_id.description: The id of the session list (8 characters).

function.name: offer_session
function.description: Use this tool first, before other tools, when the latest message of the user asks for a task that is not part of the work of this session, or that fits another session of the session list better. Do not use it for a follow-up, a correction, a question about this work, or the next step of this work: do that here. With session_id, the task goes to that existing session. Without session_id, a new session starts, nested under this session. The setting "When you ask for an unrelated task" decides: the user gets a card to choose, or the task goes there at once, or it stays here. The result tells you what to do next.

title.description: A short title of the task, for example 'Fix the login form'.

prompt.description: For a new session: the full task, because the new session has no memory of this conversation. For an existing session: the message of the user, in the words of the user.

session_id.description: The id of an existing session of the session list that fits the task better. Leave it out for a new session.

function.name: preview_servers
function.description: List the servers of .harness/launch.json of this project: the name, the state, the URL, the command, and who started it. Call it before preview_start, and before you add a server to launch.json: use a running server when it serves what you need.

function.name: preview_start
function.description: Start a server from .harness/launch.json, and wait until it is ready. With no name, start the default server. The result gives the server URL. Before you start a server, or add a new server to launch.json, call preview_servers: when a running server serves what you need, use it.

function.name: preview_stop
function.description: Stop a server of .harness/launch.json. With no name, stop all servers.

function.name: preview_logs
function.description: Read the last output lines of a server. With no name, read the default server. Use it when a server does not start, or when a request fails.

lines.description: The number of lines. The default is 50.

function.name: preview_tabs
function.description: List the tabs of the Browser pane of this session, or switch to one. You and the user use the same tabs. Before you open a page for a task, list the tabs: if the user opened a tab for this task, continue in it (give its id in 'use'), and read it with preview_snapshot. If no tab is about the task, open the page with preview_navigate and tab "new". Each tab has its id, URL, title, "shown" (the user sees it now), and "used" (you work in it).

use.description: Optional: the id of a tab to work in, or "new".

function.name: preview_navigate
function.description: Open a page in the browser. In the desktop app, this is the Browser pane of the session: you and the user use the same tabs, see the same pages, and share the cookies. With 'tab', choose the tab first: an id from preview_tabs (to continue in a tab that the user opened for this task), or "new" for a new tab (when no open tab is about this task). Without 'tab', the page opens in the tab that you used last. Give a full URL, or a path such as /about. A path opens on the current page, or on the running server. The URLs of the servers in launch.json need no approval. Other URLs need approval.

url.description: A full URL or a path.

server.description: A server name. The path opens on this server. Optional.

tab.description: Optional: a tab id from preview_tabs, or "new".

function.name: preview_snapshot
function.description: Read the page of the agent browser as a text tree. Each element that you can click or fill has a reference, for example [ref=e5]. Use this tool before preview_screenshot: text uses less context.

function.name: preview_click
function.description: Click an element of the agent browser page. Use a reference from preview_snapshot.

ref.description: The element reference, for example e5.

function.name: preview_fill
function.description: Type text into a text box of the agent browser page. The text replaces the current value. For a select box, give the option text. Use a reference from preview_snapshot.

ref.description: The element reference, for example e5.

submit.description: If true, press Enter after the text. Optional.

function.name: preview_console
function.description: Read the browser console messages of the current page: errors, failed requests, and uncaught errors. Set level to all to also get warnings and logs.

function.name: task_output
function.description: Read the new output of a background task (a bash command with run_in_background, a monitor, a background agent, or a wakeup), and its status. Each call gives only the output after the last call.

id.description: The id of the background task, for example task-1a2b3c.

wait.description: Wait at most this many seconds for the task to end (0 to 120). Optional.

function.name: task_stop
function.description: Stop a background task and all its child processes.

id.description: The id of the background task.

function.name: monitor
function.description: Run a command in the background and watch its output. Each new output line comes to you as a notification, also when no turn runs. Use it to wait for an event, for example a line in a log or the end of a deploy. Make the command print only the lines that you need (for example with grep). Stop it with task_stop when you do not need it.

command.description: The command to watch, for example a log tail or a test watcher.

description.description: What the monitor watches, in 3 to 8 words, for the user.

timeout.description: Stop the monitor after this many seconds (10 to 3600). Default: 600. Optional.

function.name: schedule_wakeup
function.description: Start a new turn later: when the time ends, you get the prompt as a notification. Use it to check a state that changes slowly and that no tool can tell you about, for example a CI run or a deploy. Do not use it to wait for a background task or a monitor: they notify you when they end.

delay_seconds.description: The time to wait, in seconds (60 to 3600).

prompt.description: The message that you get when the time ends.

reason.description: Why you wait, in 3 to 8 words, for the user.

function.name: cron_create
function.description: Schedule a prompt with a cron expression: at each time, you get the prompt as a notification, in the running turn or in a new turn. Use it when the user asks for work at set times, for example "check the deploy every 10 minutes" or "run the report at 9:00 on weekdays". A recurring task ends after 7 days. Use schedule_wakeup for one check after a delay. The tasks stay only while the session is open. List them with cron_list and stop one with cron_delete. For work that must continue after this session, use routine_create.

cron.description: 5 fields in local time: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example '*/10 * * * *' or '0 9 * * 1-5'.

prompt.description: The message that you get at each time.

recurring.description: True (default): at each time, for 7 days. False: one time only.

description.description: The task in 3 to 8 words, for the user.

function.name: cron_list
function.description: List the scheduled tasks of this session (cron_create): the id, the schedule, the next time, and the prompt.

function.name: cron_delete
function.description: Stop a scheduled task of cron_create, with its id.

function.name: routine_create
function.description: Save a routine: a prompt that Harness runs on a cron schedule, each time in a new session. Routines continue after this session ends, also when no Harness window is open. The routine shows on the Routines page, where the user can edit it, turn it off, or delete it. Use this tool when the user asks for recurring or later work that must continue after this session, for example "every morning, summarize the new commits" or "each Friday at 17:00, check the dependencies". Use cron_create only for reminders while this session is open. The runs work in the project folder of this session, with the model of this session. Use routine_list first to find a routine that does the same work. After the save, tell the user the name, the schedule, and the next run.

name.description: A short name for the Routines page, for example 'Morning commit summary'.

prompt.description: The full task for each run. A new session runs it with no memory of this conversation: give the goal, the files or commands, and what to report.

schedule.description: A cron expression with 5 fields in the local time of the daemon computer: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. For example '0 9 * * 1-5' (09:00 on weekdays).

permission_mode.description: The mode of the runs. Default: the mode of this session. It cannot be less limited than the mode of this session.

enabled.description: True (default): the routine runs on its schedule. False: it is saved as Inactive.

function.name: routine_list
function.description: List the saved routines of the Routines page: the id, the name, Active or Inactive, the schedule, the next run, the folder, and the last run. Use it before routine_create, and when the user asks about the routines.

function.name: agent
function.description:
Give a task to a subagent with a new context. It returns a report. Use it for a search or a review of many files, or for independent work. With run_in_background, you can continue your work while the subagent runs. Do not do the same work at the same time. Several agents in one step run at the same time. Select the agent type with subagent_type:
- general-purpose: For research, code search, and tasks with many steps. It has all the tools.
- Explore: A fast, read-only agent to find files and code, and to answer questions about the code. Give the search breadth in the prompt: quick, medium, or very thorough.
- Plan: A read-only software architect. It returns a plan in steps with the files to change, the risks, and the tests.

prompt.description: The full task for the subagent. It does not see this conversation.

description.description: The task in 3 to 5 words, for the user.

run_in_background.description: Return at once. The report comes to you as a notification when the subagent ends. Optional.
